Kart.metadataTitle: Market map Northern Norway — commercial property city by city | Advanti Estate
Kart.metadataDescription: Interactive market map for commercial property in Northern Norway. Compare yield, rent and vacancy city by city — Tromsø, Bodø, Alta, Narvik, Harstad and Mo i Rana — plus indicative price zones in Bodø.
Kart.lede: Choose a key figure and see how the commercial property market varies across the region. The bubbles show the level for each city — click for details and a direct path to the city's broker or full analysis.
Kart.footnoteSource: Map base: OpenStreetMap/CARTO — the bubbles show the selected key figure city by city. Price zones in Bodø are based on Advanti's own transaction and rental data, segmented by office, retail and logistics; toggle "Show property boundaries" activates Kartverket's cadastre layer. The figures are indicative estimates and do not replace a concrete valuation.
Kart.insightsIntro: The geographical picture tells more than a table. Here are the main features per {quarter}.
Kart.insight01Title: The yield requirement rises northward and inland.
Kart.insight01Body: Tromsø and Bodø have the lowest yields — greatest liquidity and deepest tenant market. Narvik and Mo i Rana are highest, where fewer transactions give a higher risk premium.
Kart.insight02Title: The rent level follows population weight.
Kart.insight02Body: Prime office rent is clearly highest in Tromsø, followed by Bodø. The difference to the smaller cities is considerable — a reflection of demand from the public sector and private business.
Kart.insight03Title: The largest markets are the tightest.
Kart.insight03Body: Tromsø has the lowest vacancy and thus the most pressure on rents. Narvik highest — but that is more about older building stock than lack of demand for class A.
Kart.ctaSub: The map shows the snapshot. In the Analytics Portal you find the development quarter by quarter, all segments and cities — with forecasts and downloadable data.
Kart.errorBody: Something went wrong while displaying the map. Try again, or go back to market insights.
Kart.noZonesNote: Price zones are currently only available for Bodø — more cities coming.
Kart.zoneValuationLink: Indicative figures — order a concrete valuation
Kart.disclaimerBodo: Zoning and prices are Advanti's indicative estimates per Q4 2025, not surveyed figures.

Shell.ariaLegend: Show or hide series in the chart
Shell.yieldAriaChart: Prime yield vs. 5-year SWAP and 10-year government bond, quarterly 2021–2025
Shell.yieldFootnote: Prime yield reflects the best property in its class — city-centre buildings with a solid tenant portfolio and long WAULT.
Shell.yieldInsight01Title: The yield peak is behind us.
Shell.yieldInsight01Body: Prime yield on office stabilized through 2024 and has corrected slightly down in 2025 — in step with falling long rates and increased buying appetite.
Shell.yieldInsight02Body: With 5-year SWAP around 3.8% and prime yield around 6.1%, the office segment has a spread of 230 bps — historically exactly what the market requires to be liquid.
Shell.yieldInsight03Body: Yield on logistics is historically high vs. office, but has moved hardest through the cycle. We expect the first significant tightening here through 2026.
Shell.leieAriaChart: Prime market rent {segment} per city, quarterly 2021–2025
Shell.leieFootnote: Market rent is prime — top rent for new build/class A in the centre. Actual average rents are 10–25% lower.
Shell.leieInsight01Body: Tromsø city centre has had 38% rent growth since 2021, driven by low new-build activity and strong public + private tenant demand.
Shell.leieInsight02Body: Bodø follows the Tromsø trend with an 18-month lag. We see considerable upside in prime office rent over the next 12 months, especially in the centre and near the railway.
Shell.leieInsight03Body: Nominal growth in 2024–25 has been driven as much by indexation as by market strength. Real growth is expected to be more moderate in 2026.
Shell.txAriaChart: Total transaction volume in Northern Norway per year, 2018–2025
Shell.txFootnote: The list shows a selection of transactions Advanti has confirmed via registration, purchase contract or directly from a party. The basis is quality-assured.
Shell.ledighetChartTitle: Share of vacant commercial space — Q4 2025
Shell.ledighetHint: Low vacancy < 4% indicates a tight market.
Shell.ledighetAriaChart: Vacancy in percent per city and segment, Q4 2025
Shell.ledighetInsight01Body: 3.4% office vacancy in Tromsø is the lowest in five years. Several public tenants have long-expired contracts and are looking for class A space.
Shell.ledighetInsight02Body: 7.5% vacancy in Narvik reflects older building stock more than lack of demand. Class A is still fully let.
Shell.ledighetInsight03Body: Vacancy in logistics is consistently low across all cities — driven by strong demand from grocery, e-commerce and industry.
Shell.kartFootnote: The map shows Advanti's six coverage cities in Northern Norway. Click a city for yield, rent and vacancy — all figures per Q4 2025.
Shell.rapporterMainBody: Complete review of yield, market rent, transaction volume and vacancy across office, retail and logistics — in all six cities we cover. 48 pages, full data package in Excel.
Shell.rapporterFootnote: The archive contains quarterly market reports and thematic deep dives. Subscription gives full access including underlying datasets.
